declarations.name: reflCocycle_eq_one_iff_const
declarations.doc: The reflection cocycle is faithful on integral multiplicative data.** For a carrier `f` that is the everywhere-valid `L`-series of an integer-valued multiplicative arithmetic function, the reflection cocycle `h_f(s) = f(1−s)/f(s)` is trivial (identically `1`) if and only if `f` is the constant `1`. No nonvanishing premise is required: cocycle triviality itself forces `f s ≠ 0` at every point, since division by zero is zero in the ambient field. Forward: `h_f(s) = 1` first forces `f s ≠ 0`, then gives `f(1−s) = f(s)`, so `f` is self-reflective and the structure theorem forces `f ≡ 1`. Backward: a constant carrier has `f(1−s)/f(s) = 1/1 = 1`.
